description.p: Kartend is a KDE-friendly Qt frontend for organizing, browsing, and launching multimedia collections with custom launchers.

It supports large libraries through virtual scrolling, asynchronous artwork loading, collection hierarchies, persistent sessions, keyboard navigation, metadata sidebars, and configurable launch commands for media, emulators, RetroArch cores, or native applications.
A collection tree, many more launchers, and a large performance pass:

ul.li: New collection tree panel — see your whole library at a glance and jump between collections, with each collection's artwork on its row
Launcher import now covers Heroic, itch.io, Bottles, and ES-DE, and collections can be built straight from Steam, Flatpak, and Lutris — with cover art fetched for them
A release split across several discs can now appear as a single item
A smart playlist can hold more than one rule
New Sidebars settings page: pick each panel's side, and whether it sits below the toolbar or runs the full window height; a sidebar can also overlap the grid instead of pushing it aside
Every scrollbar is now a three-way choice — Show, Auto-hide, or Hide — alongside a new slim overlay scrollbar style
Gamepad: the right stick drives the details pane with a ringed selection, and the shoulder buttons fold each sidebar
Uses roughly half the memory during long sessions, and moves video-frame conversion and other heavy work off the interface thread so the window stays responsive

description.p: Also includes a long list of fixes to scrolling, selection, and artwork loading.
Windows packaging fix:

ul.li: The Windows .zip and installer failed to start since 0.0.14 ("archive.dll was not found") — all required runtime DLLs are now bundled. Linux packages were unaffected.

description.p: Scraper improvements and fixes:

ul.li: Re-scrape policy, fallback region, and media quality preset can now be tuned inside the scrape window
Video and manual media types now download correctly

"Download only what's missing" now skips completed items reliably: partially-filled metadata gets completed, mixed-case artwork folders are recognised, and media a provider doesn't supply is no longer re-chased on every run
Interactive scrapes pre-filter already-complete items instead of prompting for them
Rate-limited providers are retried politely, and per-media download failures show in the completion summary
Smoother UI during large imports and scrapes, plus accessibility and stability fixes

description.p: DAT audit fix:

ul.li: When one file's content is listed by more than one catalogue entry (e.g. a non-merged clone set that re-lists a shared entry), the audit no longer reports the duplicate entry as Missing while the file is present.

description.p: Adds the DAT Manager — audit your collections against DAT files:

ul.li: See which items are present, wrong, or missing, reading inside .zip and .7z archives

A dedicated audit browser: results tree, dual detail panes, status filters, a folder-as-item view, category grouping, and saved view presets — with layout, filters, and expanded rows remembered across sessions
Clone-aware auditing with selectable Split, Merged, and Non-merged modes
One-click Fix repacks and renames archives to match the DAT; mismatched files are quarantined
DAT files can be downloaded, watched for updates, and re-downloaded in place

description.p: Also: the mouse wheel now scrolls the focused dialog, and runtime system-accent changes update every colour live.
Stability and performance release from a full-codebase audit:

ul.li: Smoother scrolling and cover flow on very large collections; cover artwork now reliably fills in
Scan and database operations retry cleanly under concurrent load; cancelling a scan no longer blocks rescanning
Search fixes: literal underscore/percent matching, no more snap-back when clearing a search quickly
Gamepad input recovers automatically after a controller disconnects or sleeps
Archive-backed items extract off-thread with a progress overlay and a decompression size cap
A persistent warning banner appears if credentials ever fall back to unencrypted storage
Play statistics are no longer lost when quitting right after launching an item

description.p: Scrape budget gets a live readout: the scrape window now shows your ScreenScraper "requests today" count alongside the time the quota resets, and once the daily request or failed-lookup quota is reported exhausted the run stops on its own instead of burning the rest of the queue.

Skip and Fill missing rescrape modes pre-filter the queue before any provider request fires: Skip drops items whose metadata is already present (database row or sidecar JSON on disk, so kart imports and older builds without a DB row are caught too); Fill missing drops items whose ticked checkboxes (metadata plus each selected media type) are all already on disk. A new "Refresh items scraped before" spinbox in scraper settings lets you mark items as eligible for refresh after a chosen number of days (default 30; 0 always skips covered items).

Settings dialog redesigned with a sidebar layout: categories live in a navigation list down the left side next to the collection tree and a new search box, replacing the previous nested rows of tabs. Draggable dividers resize the rail and split its height between the tree and the category list, and the dialog remembers its size and divider positions between runs.

Reliability and security: PDF manuals no longer crash large scrapes (non-image files are kept out of the image decoder); the scrape window's collection label updates as each collection is reached even when its items all fail; the scrape error list is scrollable and keeps far more detail; scrape logging masks ScreenScraper credentials in any URL written to scrape.log.

Pure decision logic for five managers (detail page, selection restore, attract, overlay, gamepad) extracted into helper namespaces with 102 new unit tests covering edge cases, hysteresis, boundary fallbacks, and priority ladders.

Packaging and build polish: all CMake options namespaced to KARTEND_*, portable-release flag set for distros, gamepad/SDL2/zstd auto-detect toggles, an uninstall target, CPack tarballs, a tag-triggered release workflow with sha256 publishing, hardening flags split from performance flags, and Qt 6.4 as the new minimum.

Reliability fixes: PlaylistManager export now uses QSaveFile + parent-dir fsync, failed SQL in QueryManager rescan and DbMigrations user-version writes now log instead of failing silently, PGO instrumentation actually reaches the compiler, and several Qt 6.4 portability fixes restore builds on Ubuntu 24.04.

Substantial feature release: per-collection multi-launchers with chooser dialog, splash screens with placeholder artwork, expand mode with two-stage activation, regex title-exclusion, sortable date/file size, and a configurable items-page toolbar.

Adds the Coverflow 3D view, horizontal scrolling layout, video previews and a Now Playing overlay, per-item metadata with custom fields, an artwork gallery, chronological launch history, per-item usage stats, attract mode, alias-parent links, playlists with M3U/JSON import/export, and a runtime text zoom HUD.
Packaging adds Arch PKGBUILD and a Flatpak manifest. Tests gain an integration harness for UI-coordinator managers.
Adds the attract-mode settings UI (enable toggle, idle timeout, scroll speed) and reworks the timeout reset to react to selection changes.

Settings dialog polish, expanded build-script docs, and a fix for the shutdown crash where widget-pool callbacks could outlive their targets. Adds DatabaseManager lifecycle and path-resolution unit tests.

Large refactor splitting the largest managers (Scroll, Query, Settings, Navigation, Interaction, Viewport, ItemWidget, MainWindow, SettingsDialog) into focused sibling translation units. Fixes a UBSan shutdown vptr violation and a missing include that broke the build on Ubuntu 24.04 libstdc++.

Initial release. Virtual scrolling with widget pooling, async artwork loading with disk cache, collection hierarchy with subcollection navigation, session persistence, configurable launchers, full keyboard navigation, glide scroll animations, grid and list view modes, metadata sidebar, FTS5 search, gamepad support, and Gentoo ebuild packaging.
